I would keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, that is the system I know best, it fits the climate, and it gives me the most dependable grain output with the least market risk. At my age, I would not spend energy chasing crops that need more labor, more marketing, or more technical management. I would finish the current winter wheat crop already in the field, then after harvest I would quickly plant summer maize on the same land. I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care more about stable yield and stress tolerance than saving a little on seed. For field management, I would keep fertilization moderate instead of excessive, irrigate only at the key stages, and spray only when disease or insects are likely to reduce yield. I would use rotary tillage because it is fast, familiar, and practical for me.
